*UPDATED*
REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - SEPTEMBER 22, 2022 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
COUNCILMEMBER JOHNSON WILL PARTICIPATE VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM ASTON AT THE WAIKIKI BANYAN, HOTEL LOBBY, 201 OHUA AVENUE, HONOLULU, HI 96815, AND THIS AGENDA WILL BE POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE.
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. minutes_text:
MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
SEPTEMBER 22, 2022, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA. COUNCILMEMBER JOHNSON
PARTICIPATED VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM ASTON AT THE WAIKIKI BANYAN, HOTEL
LOBBY, 201 OHUA AVENUE, HONOLULU, HI 96815, AND THE MEETING AGENDA WAS
POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT
CODE.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Dustin Parker, Concordia Lutheran Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Councilmember Naresh Solanki.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Bruce Barrows
  Mayor/Chair Chuong Vo

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council as follows:

  Pat Pacheco Insurance Agency (Business Spotlight).

5B.  Review and consideration of appointments, removals, and filling of scheduled or unscheduled
  vacancies on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (2022-24 term) (COUNCIL).

  There was no action taken on this item.

5C.  Informational update on the City’s response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other City
  events, services, and programs.

  An informational update was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no action taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  At this juncture, Bill Ihrke, City Attorney asked Councilmember Johnson to confirm for
  the record that she posted the agenda for this meeting at the location from where she
  was telephonically participating, pursuant to Brown Act requirements. Councilmember
  Johnson affirmatively confirmed.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, September 22, 2022, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 5

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Sam Desai spoke regarding the Chamber of Commerce (Chamber) State of the City
  event and inquired as to whether the Chamber quarterly report is available to the public.
  He also spoke regarding his candidacy for the ABC Unified School District Board of
  Education and expressed concerns regarding safety in the City of Cerritos.

  Bill Kalpakoff, representing Athens Services, spoke regarding service issues and offered
  assistance to customers.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Monday, September 12, 2022, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the Monday,
  September 12, 2022, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated September 22, 2022 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  September 22, 2022  $ 1,583,952.26 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING AND IMPLEMENTING TELECONFERENCE
  ACCESSIBILITY FOR CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL
  361 (STATS. 2021, CH. 165) (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, September 22, 2022, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 5

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to waive full reading of and
  adopt Resolution No. 2022-38, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING AND IMPLEMENTING
  TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY FOR CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS
  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (STATS. 2021, CH. 165) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration to authorize an annual expenditure for Integrated Library
  System (ILS) subscription software in accordance with City Purchasing and Contracting
  Policy (8.03) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Aaron Benjamin, Information Technology Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1.  Authorize the annual expenditure of $60,771.00 to Innovative Interfaces, Inc. for
  the Sierra ILS subscription software and support services in accordance with the
  Purchasing and Contracting Policy (8.03) where the purchase of goods and services
  in excess of $50,000 shall require City Council approval; and

  2.  Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute a Fiscal Year 2022-2023
  budget amendment with a new appropriation of $5,771 to be allocated for
  Innovative Interfaces, Inc. subscription software and support services (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of an exchange agreement and assignment of Federal Surface
  Transportation Program-Local and Highway Infrastructure Programs funds between the
  City of Cerritos and the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
  (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, September 22, 2022, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 5

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Deputy Director of Public Works/City Engineer.
  A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1.  Authorize the City Manager to execute the exchange agreement and assignment of
  Federal Surface Transportation Program-Local and Highway Infrastructure Programs
  Funds between the City of Cerritos and the Los Angeles County Metropolitan
  Transportation Authority in a form approved by the City Attorney; and

  2.  Authorize a budget amendment for an increase in revenues in the Street
  Improvement Fund in the amount of $247,958; and

  3.  Authorize a budget amendment for the appropriation of additional funds in the
  amount of $247,958 for Project No. 20702, Residential Pine Tree Reforestation
  Program (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Solanki, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal
  legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  Reports

11A.  Report from City Manager/Executive Director

  None.

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Reports were given by Councilmember Solanki, Mayor Pro Tem Barrows, and Mayor Vo.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, September 22, 2022, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 5

12.  Closed Session

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, announced the City Council would recess to Closed Session to
  discuss Items 12A and 12B as listed on the Closed Session agenda. Councilmember
  Johnson was not present during the Closed Session.

  12A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Consider initiation of litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code 54956.9(d)(4) (COUNCIL)
  Number of cases: One (1)

  12B.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Significant exposure to litigation
  Pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9
  (COUNCIL)
  Number of cases: One (1)

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT:

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, reported the City Council convened into Closed Session to
  discuss Items 12A and 12B, as listed on the Closed Session agenda. Councilmember
  Johnson was not present during the Closed Session. The City Council received briefings
  on the aforementioned Items and no reportable action was taken. There was nothing
  further to report.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 8:21 p.m.

  /s/Cynthia Nava
  Cynthia Nava, Assistant City Clerk/Agency Secretary
